messages.subject_clean: error in dataProcess: (sum(run.missing < 0.25) !=0) missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I looked at your data. MSstats assumes, that there two labels for each feature: L and H (or light/heavy). However, in your data each feature only has a single label. That is the source of the error.
Btw for Skyline input, you should use the censoredInt="0" option in dataProcess - only this way missing values will be handled correctly.

Kind regards,
Mateusz Staniak

messages.subject: Re: using msstats for peptide-level comparison
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

it might be technically possible - MSstats has an option for linear model-based summarization that could be used on a per-protein basis with peptide sequences in ProteinName column. But that would fit a very specific model and there's a question if that's the model you want and if it makes sense. The MSstats workflow is built around protein-level comparisons and that's where it excels.

Kind regards,
Mateusz Staniak

messages.subject: Re: Error with featureSubset = 'highQuality' and remove_uninformative_feature_outlier=TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

currently, MSstats uses broom package to process output of fitting robust linear models while performing feature selection.
However, in case of two proteins in your datasets:
- sp|O15371|EIF3D_HUMAN
- sp|P37108|SRP14_HUMAN
the model is rank deficient, and broom package returns an error in this case.
We will fix this problem in the next MSstats release. I will send you results from this version (including these two proteins in a seperate e-mail).
With the current version, excluding these two proteins from your analysis should fix the problem.

Kind regards,
Mateusz

Hi Hayley,

I think that is because of annotation for condition and bioReplicate column.
Currently, annotation is :
   Condition BioReplicate                                Run

 Condition4                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_10_15ng_270914

 Condition1                   1   QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_3_3ng_270914
 Condition2                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_4_7-5ng_270914
 Condition2                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_5_7-5ng_270914
 Condition2                   1 QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_6_7-5ng_270914
 Condition3                   1  QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_7_10ng_270914
 Condition3                   1  QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_8_10ng_270914
 Condition3                   1  QEP1_SpikeIn_230914_9_10ng_270914

Based on this information, MSstats interprets that 4 conditions come from one biological replicate, which might be paired-design.
To help MSstats recognize this design as group comparison, each condition should have different biological ID. For example, Condition1 should have BioReplicate=1, Condition2 should have BioReplicate=2, Condition3 should have BioReplicate=3 and so on.

Hope that it can help.
- Meena
